synopsis: Chapter 11 and the glossary report third-party on-demand pricing of about USD 1.861 per hour for AWS g6e.xlarge with one NVIDIA L40S; Chapter 11 specifies 4 vCPUs, 32 GiB and us-east-1 Linux pricing in 2026 [f8310, f16062, f8855]. At that rate, illustrative compute costs are USD 1,861 for 1,000 GPU-hours, USD 18,610 for 10,000 and USD 186,100 for 100,000 [f8867]. Ten instances running continuously for 122 days cost about USD 54,490 and deliver at most about 29,000 GPU-hours, excluding software licenses, storage, network egress, orchestration and support [f8869, f8868]. A one-year EC2 Instance Savings Plan lowers the quoted rate to about USD 1.17 per hour, while spot pricing is uncertain: two trackers quoted USD 0.427 and USD 1.8348 per hour [f8859, f8860]. The glossary additionally quotes about USD 30.131 per hour for eight such processors, without specifying that configuration [f16062].

relations.note: Both quote USD 1.861 hourly on demand for one L40S in US East.
